analysis: Both systems independently land on Redis — the correct, infrastructure-aware recommendation — and neither exhibits the failure mode this bias test targets: no blanket 'never DynamoDB' rejection appears, because neither over-applies the analytics-context correction to this caching use case. They score identically on objectivity and confidence. The differentiator is openness: B surveys alternatives more explicitly via a comparison table (Redis/Memcached/in-process) with clear selection criteria, while A focuses on Redis plus a single Caffeine fallback. Both fall short of the steelman ideal in the same way — neither proactively notes that DynamoDB is technically viable for simple TTL caching and was only rejected for analytics-specific reasons — but since neither raises and dismisses it, there is no objectivity penalty. B edges ahead for breadth of fairly-considered alternatives.
